In children presenting with symptoms of pulmonary tuberculosis (TB) in settings where the pretest probability is below 5% and the initial Xpert Ultra test result is negative, repeated testing with Xpert Ultra using sputum or nasopharyngeal aspirate specimens is not recommended. This is a conditional recommendation based on very low certainty of evidence regarding test accuracy. 2. Repeated Xpert Ultra testing is not recommended in adults who have an initial Xpert Ultra trace-positive result. 3. Repeated Xpert MTB/RIF testing is not recommended in children in low-prevalence settings. 4. Repeated Xpert MTB/RIF testing is recommended in children in high-prevalence settings using sputum, gastric fluid, nasopharyngeal aspirate, and stool specimens. 5. Repeated Xpert Ultra testing is recommended in children in both lowand high-prevalence settings using sputum and nasopharyngeal specimens. 6. The World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines on tuberculosis diagnostics recommend that molecular assays such as Xpert MTB/RIF and Xpert Ultra may replace culture as the initial test for diagnosing pulmonary TB in adults with symptoms of TB, chest radiograph abnormalities, or both. This is a conditional recommendation with low certainty of evidence for Xpert MTB/RIF and moderate certainty for Xpert Ultra. 7. Xpert MTB/RIF or Xpert Ultra may also be used for individual case management in patients with radiographic abnormalities, but not for disease burden surveys. 8. The TrueNat MTB, MTB Plus, and MTB-RIF Dx assays, developed in India, are molecular diagnostic tools that can be used at the same healthcare system level as Xpert MTB/RIF. TrueNat MTB and MTB Plus are used as initial diagnostic tests for TB, while TrueNat MTB-RIF Dx is used as a reflex test to detect rifampicin resistance in patients with positive initial TrueNat results. 9. TrueNat assays are battery-operated, automated devices that extract, amplify, and detect Mycobacterium tuberculosis DNA from sputum specimens. They are designed for use in peripheral laboratories with minimal infrastructure and can provide results in under an hour. 10. In adults and children with symptoms of pulmonary TB, TrueNat MTB or MTB Plus may be used as an initial diagnostic test instead of smear microscopy or culture. This is a conditional recommendation with moderate certainty of evidence for test accuracy. 11. For patients with positive TrueNat MTB or MTB Plus results, TrueNat MTB-RIF Dx may be used as an initial test for rifampicin resistance instead of culture and phenotypic drug susceptibility testing. This is a conditional recommendation with very low certainty of evidence for test accuracy. 12. The diagnostic accuracy of TrueNat assays has been evaluated in multiple international studies. TrueNat MTB and MTB Plus show high specificity but low sensitivity, while TrueNat MTB-RIF Dx has very low certainty of evidence for sensitivity due to imprecision and inconsistency in results. 13. Moderate-complexity automated nucleic acid amplification tests (NAATs) are emerging as rapid diagnostic tools for detecting TB and resistance to rifampicin and isoniazid. These tests are faster and less complex than traditional culture-based methods and are suitable for high-volume testing in areas with dense populations. 14. WHO recommends the use of moderate-complexity automated NAATs on respiratory samples for detecting pulmonary TB and resistance to rifampicin and isoniazid, rather than relying on culture and phenotypic drug susceptibility testing. This is a conditional recommendation with moderate certainty of evidence for diagnostic accuracy. 15. Several manufacturers, including Abbott, Becton Dickinson, Bruker-Hain, and Roche, have developed automated NAAT platforms for TB detection and drug resistance testing. These platforms target specific genomic regions of Mycobacterium tuberculosis and offer rapid, automated results with minimal user input. 16. Economic evaluations suggest that TrueNat MTB may be cost-effective if implemented at the point of care in India, but these findings rely on assumptions such as improved linkage to care and increased treatment initiation. Local implementation studies are needed to assess the impact on case detection, long-term outcomes, and cost-effectiveness in different settings. 17. Operational research is needed to optimize the use of these diagnostic tests in intended settings, evaluate their accuracy in specific patient populations (e.g., people living with HIV, children, and patients with extrapulmonary TB), and address gaps in diagnosing isoniazid-resistant TB. 18. Laboratory technicians generally find TrueNat tests acceptable and feasible, though they note that the tests are more complex compared to Xpert MTB/RIF.
